original_question: Suppose P(z) is a formal power series in C[[z]] with order at least 2 and with (Hes P)(0) nilpotent, so that its inversion pair Q(z) is defined by the symmetric formal map F(z) = z - grad P(z) and its formal inverse G(z) = z + grad Q(z). If P is self-inverting, meaning that its inversion pair satisfies Q(z) = P(z), must every self-inverting polynomial or formal power series automatically be Hessian nilpotent?
target_in_paper: Open Problem 4.8 (first part) in Section 4: "Decide whether or not all self-inverting polynomials or formal power series are HN."
correct_elements: The draft correctly identifies the Section 4 notion of a self-inverting series via the inversion pair Q of the symmetric map F(z)=z-∇P(z), uses the paper’s standing hypotheses o(P)≥2 and (Hes P)(0) nilpotent so that the inversion pair is defined, and asks exactly the implication that the paper isolates in the first part of Open Problem 4.8: whether self-inverting implies Hessian nilpotent. It also correctly avoids importing unrelated degree-4 or homogeneity restrictions from Conjecture 1.1, since this question belongs to the separate self-inverting discussion in Section 4.
missing_details: The number of variables should be fixed explicitly: z=(z1,...,zn) for some finite n≥1.
The ambient class should be stated cleanly as either P∈C[z] or P∈C[[z]]; the draft begins with formal power series and only later broadens to polynomials.
The paper’s HN condition means that the full Hessian matrix Hes P(z) is nilpotent as a matrix over C[z] or C[[z]], not merely that (Hes P)(0) is nilpotent.
It should be made explicit that the assumptions o(P)≥2 and (Hes P)(0) nilpotent are built into Definition 4.1 of self-inverting through the existence of the inversion pair.
If one wants the sharpest nearby reformulation, the paper proves that under these assumptions self-inverting is equivalent to ⟨∇P,∇P⟩=0, where ⟨u,v⟩=∑i uivi.
refined_question: Let n≥1 and z=(z1,...,zn). Suppose P(z) is either a polynomial in C[z] or a formal power series in C[[z]] such that o(P)≥2 and (Hes P)(0) is nilpotent, so that for the associated symmetric formal map F(z)=z-∇P(z) the formal inverse has the form G(z)=z+∇Q(z), where Q(z) is the inversion pair of P(z). If P is self-inverting, i.e. Q(z)=P(z), must P be Hessian nilpotent; equivalently, must the full Hessian matrix Hes P(z) be nilpotent?
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, by Proposition 4.3, under the same assumptions o(P)≥2 and (Hes P)(0) nilpotent, does the identity ⟨∇P,∇P⟩=0 (with ⟨u,v⟩=∑i uivi) force P to be Hessian nilpotent?
justification: The draft is clearly targeting Section 4 rather than the main vanishing-conjecture material from Section 1: it uses the paper’s exact self-inverting setup from Definition 4.1 and asks precisely whether self-inverting implies HN. That matches the first clause of Open Problem 4.8 almost verbatim. The nearby context that makes the question stand-alone is Definition 4.1 for self-inverting, Proposition 4.2 for quasi-translations, Proposition 4.3 for the equivalent criterion ⟨∇P,∇P⟩=0, and the Section 1.1 discussion (especially Proposition 1.2 and Theorem 1.3) that fixes the inversion-pair notation and hypotheses. The second clause of Open Problem 4.8 is a different question, namely classification of HN self-inverting objects, so it should not be merged into the refined question.
